method: Direct browser playback, pause and UI frame stepping. Times are approximate player timestamps; no native source FPS, 3D angles, grip distances or exact impact measurements inferred.

sources.title: Monster Hunter Wilds: Great Sword | Weapon Overview
sources.creator: Monster Hunter / Capcom

observations.note: Hunter lowered with large blade raised diagonally before the cut.
Blade carried very low to the side after the cut; trunk follows the action.
Low follow-through and dust; monster obscures the exact contact.
Hunter lifts/levers the large blade out of the low position to continue.
Blade borne behind/right shoulder; free support hand.
Chest rocks back and weapon loads behind the body.
Blade raised behind/above shoulder, still preparing.
Broad forward/downward release, torso and legs turn with the blade.
Blade finishes low/outside, chest folds forward to follow and brace.
Body rocks back and blade remains low/behind while counter-loading the next cut.

adaptation.intent: Original exaggerated full-effort R6 heavy sword combo. Observed heavy footage guides load, overswing, low finish and effortful recovery; previous measured R6 source supplies only rig mechanics.
adaptation.grip: Dominant hand attached. Support hand joins powered phases and releases into low recovery as a deliberate game-style choice. Footage does not establish mandatory release for all heavy swords.
adaptation.timing: At 60 FPS choose 26-28 frames Hit-to-overswing and 36-50 recovery frames, informed by DS3 visible release near 5.77, low finish near 6.2 and counter-load near 6.8. These are authored retimings, not a frame retarget.
adaptation.r6Limits: No knees/elbows, so modest stance depth with planted soles and thigh clearance; body effort expressed by torso turn/lean, load and weapon path.
